title: Usage Insights: export job service + download endpoint (CSV/JSON) w/ size limits + retries
author: Chloe Martin
description:
Context: Usage Insights needs an exportable report (CSV + JSON) that customers can attach to FinOps workflows and incident/cost reviews. This PR adds the export job service (create/poll/download) and formatting for the route/model cost driver aggregates. It also introduces hard guardrails (row/bytes/time-range) and retry logic to reduce timeouts seen in internal load tests and in SUP-18458.

What’s in this PR: (1) New API endpoints: POST /v1/usage-insights/exports creates an async export job; GET /v1/usage-insights/exports/{export_id} returns job status + metadata; GET /v1/usage-insights/exports/{export_id}/download streams the file (CSV or JSON) when ready. (2) Export query + formatting: Export pulls from the existing usage-insights aggregate views (hourly/daily rollups) and writes a bounded report in either CSV or JSON. CSV is header-stable and uses a deterministic column order; JSON is newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) for streaming/large files. (3) Guardrails: max time window 31 days; max rows 250,000; max uncompressed output size ~50 MiB (enforced during generation); request-level validation returns 400 with a typed error when exceeded. (4) Reliability improvements: export worker uses idempotency key (org_id + project_id + filters hash) to avoid duplicate work from client retries; generation step has bounded retries with exponential backoff on transient warehouse/object-store errors; download endpoint supports Range requests for resumable downloads.

Non-goals / follow-ups: Audit logging events and stricter RBAC enforcement are handled in PR-15492 (this PR adds the required plumbing fields on the export job record but does not emit audit events yet). Scheduled exports are explicitly out-of-scope for GA.

Implementation notes: Export jobs are persisted in postgres (usage_insights_export_jobs). File payload is written to object storage (exports/{org_id}/{project_id}/{export_id}.{csv|ndjson}) with server-side encryption enabled. The download endpoint authenticates the caller, verifies org/project scope, checks job ownership, and then streams from object storage to avoid loading entire exports in memory. The worker emits metrics: export_job_created_total, export_job_completed_total, export_job_failed_total, export_job_duration_seconds, export_job_bytes_written, and export_job_rows_written.

Testing: Unit tests for validation and formatting; integration tests covering create->poll->download flow; load-test harness run locally against staging warehouse with large exports to confirm size limits and that retries do not exceed job timeout.

Customer impact: Enables manual exports from the console/UI. Customers may see errors for overly-large time ranges; error messages include suggested mitigations (shorter range, filters, or paginated exports via API in a follow-up).

usage-insights/export: implement export worker (csv + ndjson writers)
api: add export endpoints + request validation
storage: add object store streaming helper + Range support
tests: add integration tests for export lifecycle
docs(internal): add export limits + error codes to API contract stub
conversation: Jada Williams (review): Can we make the export output schema explicit/stable? Customers will automate against it and we can’t reshuffle columns without a versioning story. Also, why NDJSON instead of JSON array?

Chloe Martin (author): Good call. Updated CSV writer to use a fixed column list + deterministic ordering; added a unit test asserting header + column order. NDJSON chosen for streaming + avoiding huge in-memory arrays; download is still “application/json” for NDJSON and documented as newline-delimited. I added response header `X-Redwood-Export-Format: ndjson` to make it explicit.
Allison Grant (review): Size limits look reasonable, but the failure mode should be clear. If we hit the byte limit mid-stream, do we produce a truncated file? That’s risky.

Chloe Martin (author): Agreed. Changed behavior: we preflight with an upper-bound row estimate, and during generation we hard-fail before uploading final object (we write to a temp key and only promote on success). If the byte counter exceeds max, job transitions to FAILED with error_code=EXPORT_TOO_LARGE and we delete the temp object.

Kevin Osei (review): We need to be careful about org/project isolation and exporting across environments. I don’t see audit logging yet, but at least confirm the job record includes org_id/project_id + the exact filters and requester identity so PR-15492 can emit audit events.

Chloe Martin (author): Yep. Job table now stores org_id, project_id, created_by_user_id, created_by_api_key_id (nullable), requested_at, filter_hash, filters_json, time_window_start/end, environment, region, format, and limits_applied. RBAC enforcement is currently the existing project-scoped auth middleware; audit events will be added in 15492.
Mei Lin (review): Can we ensure the export query matches the aggregates used by the UI? Otherwise customers will reconcile a different number.

Chloe Martin (author): Export pulls from the same rollup views as the UI endpoints (route/model aggregates). I added integration coverage asserting that exporting a small fixture dataset matches the API route list totals for the same filter set.
Paula Mendes (PM): Please add a user-facing error message for ‘time range too large’ that suggests “31 days max” and points to filters. Support will need something consistent.

Chloe Martin (author): Added error_message strings for EXPORT_TIME_RANGE_TOO_LARGE / EXPORT_TOO_MANY_ROWS / EXPORT_TOO_LARGE, plus docs notes in the API type definitions. UI strings will land in the console PR.
Kevin Osei (approval): Approved with note: ensure PR-15492 adds audit events for create + download and includes the filter payload in the event body.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Please add an alert in observability pack for export_job_failed_total rate once metrics are wired (ENG-8430).
Jada Williams (approval): Approved. Thanks for pinning the header ordering + adding schema tests.
